subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

Hi John -

Thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Call recap (top-level):
- Legacy Bank is targeting a private, air-gapped on-prem deployment for customer-facing features (no external egress).
- Primary concerns: hardware spec (GPU count/model), offline model ingestion, upgrade/patch process in an air-gapped environment, KMS/HSM integration, and operational monitoring without external telemetry.
- Desired schedule: goal to have a small functional PoC in Q1 and a phased production roll in Q2, pending procurement and security review.

Questions we left on the table (please confirm):
1) Hardware: you mentioned an existing DGX-like rack and a preference for H100s - can you confirm target GPU count per cluster (e.g., 4x, 8x, 16x) and whether NVMe removable carriers will be used for model transfer?
2) Models & performance: what model families are you planning to run (internal fine-tuned LLM, Llama2, etc.) and an initial perf target (concurrent sessions / QPS / p99 latency target)?
3) Upgrades: you mentioned offline upgrades. Do you require signed packages only (we support signed tarballs / rpm/deb artifacts) and will your infra team perform the staging and validation? Also, desired rollback window?
4) Security: confirm SOC2/PCI applicability and any additional audit evidence you'll need (audit logs retention, HSM attestations).

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll send our on-prem hardware guidance and checklist (attached) - this includes recommended GPU counts, network layout, and storage guidance.
- Technical workshop: schedule a 60-90min session with your infra/SRE + our SRE (Dylan) and Security (Rishi) to walk the offline upgrade flow and model ingestion runbook. Proposed dates: Tue 12/7 or Thu 12/9.
- PoC scope: start with a 1-GPU functional PoC (model load, inference, offline ingest) to validate offline procedures before scaling to a multi-GPU performance run.
- Legal/Procurement: Monica will share the mutual action plan and typical timeline for private deployments once we confirm scope.

Please see attached: redwood_onprem_hwg_v1.pdf (hardware guidance / checklist).

If you can reply with the answers to 1-4 above and confirm a workshop date, we'll get the MMP and PoC plan out same day.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood_onprem_hwg_v1.pdf (document stub - hardware guidance)

From: John Smith <john.smith@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@legacybank.com, Legacy Bank Security <sec@legacybank.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

Marissa -

Thanks for the recap. Answers below:

1) Hardware: we currently have a 32-slot rack (DGX-like). For the initial deployment we are planning 4x H100 per node for the PoC and will scale to 8-16 GPUs per cluster for production. We will use encrypted removable NVMe carriers for model transfers (we have a validated workflow for FIPS-compliant SSDs).

2) Models & perf: initial models will be an internal fine-tuned Llama2-13B variant for contextual customer responses. Target for PoC is functional validation (single-node). Production target: ~150 concurrent sessions, p50 < 100ms for short prompts, p95 ~ 250-300ms depending on batching. We can provide sample prompt mixes.

3) Upgrades: yes - we require signed artifacts (our security team will validate signatures). Our infra team will stage and apply updates during scheduled maintenance windows (monthly), with a 24hr rollback window for critical fixes. We cannot accept any process that requires external internet access from the inference nodes.

4) Security: SOC2 and PCI are both in scope. We'll need audit evidence for model access logs, operator actions, and KMS attestations. We have an internal checklist we can share.

I attached our current hardware inventory spreadsheet for reference. Happy to lock a workshop on 12/7 - 10am PT works for our infra lead.

-John
John Smith
Director, Platform Engineering | Legacy Bank
john.smith@legacybank.com | +1 212-555-0199

Attachment: legacy_hw_inventory.xlsx (inventory stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@legacybank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

John / Marissa -

Thanks - helpful details. A few technical clarifications from the infra side so we can size the PoC and the production cluster correctly: 

- GPU and memory: H100s are fine. Please confirm target GPU memory footprint for your model family (13B with typical sequence lengths -> estimate ~24-30GB KV per session).
- NVMe usage: confirm whether removable NVMe will be hot-plugged by your team or staged offline and mounted for ingestion. We support both flows but the ingestion tooling differs (streaming copy vs local mount ingest).
- Kernel/driver freeze: for air-gapped infra we need a driver/kernel matrix to validate CUDA/cuDNN compatibility. Can you share the OS version and kernel policy (do you allow security-only backports)?
- Monitoring: if nodes cannot export telemetry externally, we can run a local Prometheus exporter and create a pull-forward job that exports meta-metrics via signed bundles during maintenance windows. Would that meet audit needs?
- Model packaging: we support signed model bundles and a verification step that runs locally before model load. We'll share an offline-ingest-runbook that covers checksums, signatures, and verification steps.

I've attached a short runbook for the offline ingestion path - will expand based on your feedback.

If 12/7 10am PT works, I'll use the session to walk through the ingestion flow and upgrade/rollback steps with your infra lead and security.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Attachment: offline-ingest-runbook.md (runbook stub)

Hi John -

Appreciate the detailed answers - that gives us enough to move forward. Quick consolidated next steps and asks so we're aligned before the workshop on 12/7 10am PT: 

Short immediate asks for your infra/security teams: 
- Confirm final GPU counts for PoC (you indicated 4x H100).
- Share OS/kernel version and any driver policy (security-only backports vs full upgrades).
- Provide a short sample prompt set (we'll use this to run latency profiling during PoC).
- Share your internal checklist for audit evidence (Rishi will pre-read to map to our logging/attestation features).

Planned deliverables from Redwood ahead of the workshop: 
- Mutual action plan (Monica will send MMP and legal checklist after this thread).
- On-prem hardware guidance (attached earlier) and a tailored checklist for H100s.
- Offline ingest runbook (Dylan attached a starter runbook; we'll expand it based on your kernel/driver policy).
- Proposed PoC scope: 1-node functional validation (model ingest, inference, offline log bundling) -> if successful, plan a perf run on a 4-GPU node.

We'll also map security evidence items during the workshop and confirm a target timeline for the PoC sign-off (proposed: 4 weeks from PoC start).

Please confirm the 12/7 10am PT workshop and reply with the four asks above at your earliest convenience. Monica and Rishi will join the workshop to kick off MMP and security mapping.

Thanks - talk soon.
